classification.difficultyReason: Derive the supplied balance expression using the taught series method, set the balance to zero and rearrange for principal with downward rounding.

content.prompt: A couple have worked out that they can afford to pay $\$19\,200$ each year in mortgage payments. The current home loan rate is 7.5% per annum, with equal payments made monthly over a period of 25 years.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Let $P$ be the principal borrowed and $A_{300}$ the amount owing after 25 years. Show that
$$A_{300}=P\times1.00625^{300}-\frac{1600(1.00625^{300}-1)}{0.00625}.$$

answer.worked:
Monthly repayment:
$$\frac{19200}{12}=\$1600.$$
Monthly growth factor:
$$r=1+\frac{0.075}{12}=1.00625.$$
Number of repayments:
$$n=25\times12=300.$$
Start: $P$.

After the first repayment:
$$A_1=Pr-1600.$$
After the second repayment:
$$\begin{aligned}A_2&=(Pr-1600)r-1600\\A_2&=Pr^2-1600r-1600.\end{aligned}$$
After 300 repayments:
$$A_{300}=Pr^{300}-1600r^{299}-1600r^{298}-\cdots-1600.$$
The repayment terms form a geometric series with first term $1600$, common ratio $r$ and 300 terms.
$$\begin{aligned}A_{300}&=Pr^{300}-1600\frac{r^{300}-1}{r-1}\\A_{300}&=P(1.00625)^{300}-\frac{1600(1.00625^{300}-1)}{0.00625}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence determine the maximum amount that the couple can borrow and still pay off the loan. Round your answer down to the nearest dollar.
